symptom: A pluggable widget exposing several datasources cannot be authored: naming one by its schema key is MDL-WIDGET05, and the generic `datasource:` clause fills only one of them (which one was decided by Go map iteration order, so the same script produced different documents)
cause: Three places assumed one datasource per widget: `datasourceTypedKeys` rejected every named datasource-typed key regardless of the VALUE's shape, `resolveMapping`'s DataSource case read only `w.GetDataSource()`, and `hasDataSource` was a widget-wide check so a named datasource could not select the mode that owns it. A fourth, MDL-WIDGET16, read only the generic clause and so contradicted WIDGET05 on the same widget
insight: MDL-WIDGET05 must judge the VALUE's shape, not the key: a *ast.DataSourceV3 under a datasource key is the fix, a scalar there is still #643's silent drop. Aliases belong in the key set or the scalar reaches the same drop by the other spelling. Refuse an ambiguous generic clause rather than guess -- both guesses are wrong (fan out = duplicated binding, first-only = CE0642 on a property nobody mentioned). When adding a spelling, grep for EVERY validator with the old assumption: WIDGET16 was missed until an example fixture failed, and two validators disagreeing blocks exec entirely. The explicit-property fallback needed no change: its type switch already `continue`s on a non-scalar, so a named datasource cannot be double-applied
